newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign bank puts money in China interbank market.
newsitem.headline: Foreign bank puts money in China interbank market.

text.p: The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi said on Monday it had become the first foreign bank to deposit in China's local currency interbank market, a bank official said.

The official said the deposit, only possible for foreign banks with approval to do yuan business, was handled by the Shanghai Short-term Financing Centre, a money brokerage run by the central bank and a full member of the interbank market.
The deposit of 10 million yuan was placed on 18-day deposit at an annual rate of 10.98 percent, the official said.
Until now foreign banks have only been allowed to make small transactions of a maximum of 48 hours through the yuan interbank market to cover settlement of accounts by foreign-funded firms.
The Tokyo-Mitsubishi official said the bank had used its own capital for the deposit.
He said foreign banks would be allowed to both lend and borrow from the yuan interbank market but with strict limits.
"We expect to be in the market regularly, but the amounts are limited by the central bank," the official said. "But the market welcomes us."
He declined to give the limits set by the central bank for deposits and lending by foreign banks from the interbank market.
He also said Tokyo-Mitsubishi would make several Chinese yuan loans to customers on Monday, probably making it the first foreign bank to actually conduct yuan loan business.
The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp and the Industrial Bank of Japan announced the start of yuan business last week, but only referred to loan pre-agreements.
"These are not pre-agreements, this is real business," said the Tokyo-Mitsubishi official.
A total of eight foreign banks in Shanghai have been aproved to do local yuan business on a limited scale.
